articles.title: India steps up space ambitions, eyes crewed missions and space station
articles.summary: India has gained valuable human spaceflight experience through international cooperation, most notably with Shukla becoming the first Indian to visit the International Space Station last year. Serving as a pilot, his mission underscores India's growing involvement in global space endeavors. This achievement is a significant step, paving the way for future Indian-led space missions and further enhancing the nation's capabilities in space exploration.

articles.title: Delhi building collapse: HC seeks govt's reply on hostel facilities for DU
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has requested responses from the Central Government, Delhi Government, and Delhi University regarding a plea by the NSUI president. The plea advocates for mandatory hostel facilities in all Delhi University colleges. This development highlights ongoing discussions about student welfare and infrastructure within higher education institutions, prompting judicial review into accessibility and resources for students in the capital.

articles.title: Beneath New York’s water system lies an 85-mile underground river that carries roughly half the city’s drinking water — parts of it run more than a thousand feet below ground and are so inaccessible that engineers inspect them with robotic submarines
articles.summary: New York City relies on a crucial 85-mile underground "hole in the rock" infrastructure, largely unseen by the public. This vital system connects reservoirs in the Catskills, serving as the primary water supply for millions of residents. It exemplifies essential urban engineering and planning critical for major metropolitan areas.

articles.title: Manitoba Hydro hearings conclude with more criticism of plan to burn more natural gas
articles.summary: Public hearings in Manitoba, Canada, regarding Manitoba Hydro's proposed natural gas expansion in Brandon have concluded after six weeks. The initiative by the Crown corporation faced considerable criticism during the proceedings, overseen by the Public Utilities Board. This development underscores the complex interplay between energy infrastructure projects, public opinion, and regulatory oversight in resource management within a nation.

articles.title: Mail-in voters weigh flying to vote in person and other backup plans amid uncertainty
articles.summary: Kelsi Kiper, spouse of an active-duty service member, has consistently used the U.S. Postal Service for almost a decade to cast her ballots. Registered in Texas but stationed out of state, her reliance on mail-in voting highlights the critical role of postal services in facilitating electoral participation for military families. This mechanism ensures service members and their dependents can exercise their democratic rights despite frequent relocations.
